content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Active Reconnaissance and Footprinting (Nmap, Masscan)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Active reconnaissance involves interacting directly with a target system to gather detailed information about its network architecture, live hosts, open ports, and running services. Unlike passive reconnaissance, active methods generate network traffic that can potentially be detected by intrusion detection systems (IDS) and firewalls."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Masscan for High-Speed Port Scanning"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Masscan is an Internet-scale port scanner that can transmit packets asynchronously at rates of up to 10 million packets per second. It uses a custom TCP stack similar to optimal mass-scanning tools, making it ideal for mapping large networks or the entire Internet in minutes."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"masscan 192.168.1.0/24 -p1-65535 --rate=1000"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"192.168.1.0/24: Specifies the target subnet to scan."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-p1-65535: Scans all 65,535 TCP ports."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--rate=1000: Limits the transmission rate to 1000 packets per second to prevent network congestion."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Comprehensive Enumeration with Nmap"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"While Masscan excels at identifying live ports quickly, Nmap (Network Mapper) provides deep, accurate service and OS fingerprinting capabilities. Nmap uses various techniques like SYN scans, UDP scans, and script scanning to deeply profile the target."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"nmap -sS -sV -O -p- 192.168.1.50"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-sS: Performs a TCP SYN stealth scan, which is the default and most popular scan option."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-sV: Probes open ports to determine service and version info."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-O: Enables operating system detection."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-p-: Scans all ports from 1 to 65535."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Leveraging Nmap Scripting Engine (NSE)"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Nmap Scripting Engine allows ethical hackers to write and share scripts in Lua to automate a wide variety of networking tasks, from vulnerability detection to exploitation."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"nmap --script vuln 192.168.1.50"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The --script vuln flag loads all scripts in the vulnerability category to check the target for known security flaws."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices and Safety"},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always obtain explicit written permission before conducting active reconnaissance against any network."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Adjust scan rates to avoid overwhelming fragile legacy systems or triggering denial-of-service conditions."}]
